questions.q: Which matrices have a singular value decomposition A = UΣV^T?
options: Only square matrices
Only symmetric matrices
Only invertible matrices
Any real matrix, regardless of its shape
questions.explain: Unlike eigendecomposition, the SVD exists for every real matrix, whether it is square, rectangular, symmetric, or singular.

questions.q: What is the relationship between the singular values of A and the eigenvalues of A^T A?
options: Singular values equal the eigenvalues of A^T A directly
Singular values are the square roots of the eigenvalues of A^T A
Singular values are unrelated to A^T A
Singular values equal the trace of A^T A
questions.explain: Because A^T A = VΣ^TΣV^T, the columns of V are eigenvectors of A^T A, and each singular value satisfies σ_i = sqrt(λ_i(A^T A)).

questions.q: Why are singular values always real and non-negative, even for a matrix that is not square or symmetric?
options: Because all matrix entries are assumed non-negative
Because singular values are square roots of eigenvalues of A^T A, which is always symmetric positive semi-definite
Because singular values are arbitrarily defined to be positive
Because A is always invertible
questions.explain: A^T A is guaranteed to be symmetric positive semi-definite for any A, so its eigenvalues are real and non-negative, and taking square roots preserves that.

questions.q: According to the Eckart-Young theorem, what does truncating the SVD to its top k singular values give you?
options: A random rank-k matrix unrelated to A
The best possible rank-k approximation of A in the least-squares sense
The exact inverse of A
A matrix with the same rank as A but different singular values
questions.explain: The Eckart-Young theorem states that truncating the SVD to the k largest singular values and corresponding singular vectors produces the provably optimal rank-k approximation of A.

questions.q: In the worked example with a 4-day, 2-asset returns matrix X, what does the first right singular vector represent?
options: The day with the largest single return
The direction in asset-return space carrying the most variance across the observed days
The average return of both assets
The determinant of X
questions.explain: The first right singular vector points in the direction of greatest variance in the data, which is exactly the first principal component computed in the next lesson's PCA.
